children: STOCKHOLM--Volvo Car is closing its Stockholm office as it moves to focus its resources in Sweden across fewer sites to increase efficiency.

The majority of the responsibilities undertaken by the Stockholm office will be shifted to the Swedish automaker's headquarters in Gothenburg on the west coast of the country, it said in a statement Monday.
The move comes as it continues to work on cutting costs, with the company grappling with higher expenses and a Chinese auto market beset with intense competition and pricing pressure.
After completing an 18 billion Swedish kronor ($1.87 billion) cost-saving plan in 2025, it recently concluded measures to save a further 5 billion kronor.

Monday's decision to close its Stockholm office is aimed at creating a more focused organization, reducing complexity and increasing collaboration as it seeks to strengthen competitiveness in an increasingly challenging market, it said.

The Stockholm office was established to access critical talent and strengthen key capabilities in areas including software development, AI and digital customer experiences. Around 450 Volvo Car workers are currently based in the office. The company didn't specify whether those affected would be laid off or offered transfers.
The transition to Gothenburg will take place gradually until the office closes on March 1, Volvo said.
